methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $60M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
REGENT Craft is a Series A-stage transportation company that has raised $60M to date. The broader transportation sector comp universe includes six private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, FleetZero, Beyond Aero) and no public comparables; however, no subset of same-stage or adjacent-stage peers with sufficient data density exists to support peer-median valuation.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach. Using total capital raised ($60M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement yields $120M. This reflects the standard expectation that post-Series A valuations step up meaningfully from deployed capital, accounting for early operational progress and reduced execution risk relative to seed stage.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $102M to $138M, with a median point of $120M. The range reflects reasonable upside and downside variance around the stage-progression result, though with only one methodological anchor, conviction is constrained. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrowly-filtered Transportation peers at similar stage and scale—which limits cross-validation—and the opacity of REGENT Craft's unit economics, capital efficiency, and competitive positioning relative to the broader mobility ecosystem. Additional data on revenue trajectory, burn rate, or customer traction would materially sharpen the valuation band.
